me_southern_boulder_patch.blurb: A small cluster of granite boulders in the woods at Bradbury Mountain State Park, in the Greater Portland part of southern Maine. They are the first blocks a climber meets when walking in from the south. There are 11 problems, all bouldering, spread from the easiest grades up to a handful in the V3 to V6 range, so there is something for most visitors. The boulders are short rather than towering, with plenty of enjoyable lines, and the grain of the granite is coarse and sharp on the skin. Bring a pad and tape, and expect a walk through forest to reach them rather than a roadside stop.

_expect.name: Crocodile Blocs (South side of river, downriver of bridge)

me_crocodile_blocs_south_side_of_river_d.blurb: Three separate faces strung along the south bank of the river below the bridge at Lisbon Falls, in Maine's Midcoast. The area holds 11 boulder problems that run from easy ones up through a solid middle band of V3 and V5 lines to a single hard project near the top of the scale. The first face sits right at the bottom of the embankment, the next is a short stroll downstream, and the third lies roughly 150 feet past that, so a session here is a compact riverside circuit. It pairs well with the other boulders nearby for an afternoon outing.

me_boulder_field.blurb: A wide talus slope strewn with boulders beneath the cliff line at Bear Mountain, just south of Waterford in western Maine, overlooking Bear Pond. It holds 11 boulder problems on the V-scale, from a friendly V1 warm-up slab near the bottom to a V7 at the top end, with most of the good lines in the V2 to V6 band. A few of the problems are well regarded and draw repeat visits. There is no marked trail through the blocks; you pick your own way uphill among the rocks, so wear sturdy shoes and bring pads. The cliff above also offers sport, trad and ice for mixed days.
me_boulder_field.parking_note: Leave the car at the boat launch beside Bear Pond on Route 37, then cross the road to reach the boulders.

me_dodge_point.blurb: A short, steep, tucked-away boulder wall within Dodge Point Preserve, about three miles south of Damariscotta and Newcastle on the Damariscotta River. Eleven problems climb small crimps with decent footholds and usually end on mossy top-outs, so it rewards finger strength. The grades are widely spaced, from V0 and V1 up through the middle range of V3 to V7 and one very hard line near V10. It sits roughly a mile in along forest trails rather than near the car, so treat it as a short hike with pads, and expect damp conditions after rain.

me_a_maple_run_wall.blurb: The first wall on the left as you reach the cliff at Parks Pond Bluff in Clifton, Maine. It holds ten routes, almost all bolted sport lines plus a single trad climb, and nearly everything is 5.11 or 5.12 with one 5.9 for balance. The climbing is steep and pumpy on positive edges, a contrast to the scruffier, slabbier faces nearby. The wall was cleaned thoroughly before the routes were bolted, so the lines are clean. It suits strong sport climbers more than beginners, and a few routes date to the early 1990s.
me_a_maple_run_wall.parking_note: Pull off at the small grassy pullout on the right side of Route 9, about 2.7 miles east of the Route 180 junction and past Parks Pond on your right; it fits only a few cars.

me_bear_cub_cliff_gilead_me.blurb: A small crag in Gilead, western Maine, a short distance before the main Tumbledown Dick cliffs, on schist. The ten climbs are mostly traditional routes from easy fifth-class up to about 5.10, with one aid line and a short boulder problem. A few of the routes are well liked. Reaching the base takes real effort: the trail climbs steeply up the hillside following cairns and flagging, passes boulders, and finishes with a scramble through blocks along the cliff. Do not expect a busy scene or a smooth path, and bring a rack with you.

me_burried_treasure_boulder.blurb: One big block sitting in a sunken pit in the middle of The Spot, the best bouldering in Camden Hills State Park, on the rock the park is known for: gneiss, which grips well but can be sharp. The boulder carries ten problems, all between V1 and V4. Two of them, a V1 mantel and a V2 on the downhill face, are regarded as the best, and the V4s add a stiffer test. It makes a friendly stop for climbers in the easy-to-moderate range. Bring a couple of pads, and expect a sunny spot with a steep scramble up a gully to get there.
